findings.title: Cleanup success path logs full ID lists at error level
findings.body: CleanAnnotations and CleanOrphanedAnnotationTags call r.log.Error on every batch, including when the fetch returns no rows and err is nil (lines 534, 537, 554, 557, 576, and 579). Each call dumps the entire ID slice and the SQL condition. These run before the empty-batch stop, so every cleanup cycle emits error logs even when nothing is deleted, and a large backlog emits two error lines per batch with tens of thousands of IDs. That floods logs, looks like a failing job to anything alerting on error level, and can stall the cleaner on log serialization. These look like leftover diagnostics and should be removed, or reduced to debug without the ID list.

findings.title: Global cleanup interval accidentally cut from 10 minutes to 1
findings.body: Run now uses time.NewTicker(time.Minute * 1) instead of 10 minutes. This is unrelated to the annotation deadlock fix and is not described in the PR. It schedules every cleanup job (snapshots, dashboard versions, images, annotations, invites, short URLs, query history) ten times as often. clean() is synchronous with a 9-minute timeout chosen for the old 10-minute cadence; if a pass takes longer than a minute the ticker's buffered tick starts the next pass immediately, so a busy instance can run cleanup continuously and multiply DB load. Restore the 10-minute interval unless a faster schedule is an intentional, documented change.

findings.title: SQLite ID list is built with quadratic string concatenation
findings.body: When the DB is SQLite and AnnotationCleanupJobBatchSize exceeds 999, deleteByIDs inlines every ID with values = fmt.Sprintf("%s, %d", values, v) in a loop. Each step copies the whole string, so a batch of N IDs copies O(N^2) bytes. The new test uses batch size 32767, which is on this path and copies on the order of gigabytes of temporary strings, adding multi-second latency and GC pressure exactly when the batch is large. Build the IN list with strings.Builder (or chunks) instead.
